blocks.x: Exceptions auto-resolved at 74% — control tower to agentic remediation
A global 3PL (40+ countries) — Logistics & Supply Chain engagement delivered by a 19-person team over 14 months, Global scope, commercial model: outcome-linked.

items: Visibility stitched from carrier portals; ETAs updated by phone.
Exception queues consumed 60% of ops capacity.

blocks.x: The event spine unified TMS/WMS/telematics/carrier events on Forge; Nexus decision policies route exceptions; Swarm agents remediate the recoverable classes (document mismatches, rebookings, detention claims) within policy. Carrier identity verification closed the fraud vector.

The cadence, without the ceremony: weeks 1–2 produce the signed baseline: current per lane performance, method note, and a control owner who co-signs every later claim. the middle block runs the pilot against live WMS floor systems data at deliberately small scope: one path, one team, one region, expanded only after its eval gate holds. The part that survives audit is the boring part: identity is short-lived and authorization is deny-by-default in Data, Analytics & Lakehouse delivery, so your control owners can interrogate any number we publish.. The engineering bet is explicit: every state change is replayable from the signed baseline on Data, Analytics & Lakehouse programs, so drift shows up as a ticket with an owner, not as a mystery.

items: Current programs land 10x here; the gate reviews the live number, not a projection
The engineering bet is explicit: each stage owns its latency budget and its failure policy in A global 3PL (40+ countries), and every exception path degrades to human review, never to silence.

blocks.x: Towers: Agentic AI & Hyperautomation, Data, Analytics & Lakehouse, Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust. Platforms: Dataq Swarm, Dataq Nexus, Dataq Forge.

items: Engineered for Logistics & Supply Chain from day one: contracts first, runbooks shipped with the working slice

What holds the build together is discipline at the boundaries: signals cross boundaries only through typed contracts in Data, Analytics & Lakehouse delivery, so the question of how we know gets a pointer, not a paragraph.
